assets.prompt:
Use case: identity-preserve.
Make a very small local refinement of the lower-lip-to-chin transition in Image 1, the edit target, to harmonize with the already-refined FRONT portrait in Image 2.

IMAGE ROLES:
Image 1 determines the entire output: exact profile angle, identity, head silhouette, facial proportions, expression, pose, hairstyle, eye color, lighting, clothes, background and crop.
Image 2 is ONLY a reference for a more continuous chin surface without a separated block-like chin pad. Do NOT copy its front-facing angle, facial width, mouth shape, head tilt, expression or lighting.

LOCAL CHANGE:
In Image 1, make the short transition from the natural hollow below the lower lip into the front of the chin slightly smoother and more continuous. Gently reduce the abrupt convex shoulder of the chin pad that makes it look like a separate rounded block. Keep the natural labiomental hollow; do not fill it flat or erase it. The change is subtle surface shaping, consistent with the understated adult chin in Image 2.

Keep the chin in the same overall position with essentially the same projection, height and size. Preserve the nose-lip-chin balance, the location of the lips and existing slight lip separation. Do NOT push the chin backward, shorten or narrow the lower face, round the jaw, make a pointed chin, or exaggerate the lip projection. Preserve the defined adult jawline and posterior jaw angle.

Preserve all non-target features as closely as possible: the identical right-facing profile view, eye and brow shape, focused reserved gaze, muted pale gray-blue irises, apparent age, skin tone and fine texture, short dark waves, neck/shoulders, original lighting direction and contrast, black clothing and dark architectural setting. Do not brighten the face, alter the expression, rotate the head or introduce front-view details. No skin beautification, added wrinkles, text or accessories. One photorealistic color portrait in the same vertical 3:4 frame.
